## Objective
- Expand the existing RING//RIOT fighting game with triple jumps, faster movement, double-tap K spin kicks, face uploads, and an online lobby to find and challenge players.

## Requirements
- Build a complete playable game or apply the requested changes without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide); read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implement browser-local online discovery and duels using `BroadcastChannel`; players can find each other in separate tabs on the same browser, but this is not internet-wide multiplayer.
- Keep the existing CPU fight as the default and add challenges from the lobby.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added triple-jump physics, faster movement, and double-tap K spin kicks with touch controls.
- Added an online lobby, player presence discovery, challenge/accept flow, and state/damage synchronization.
- Added lobby and control styling; face upload was already present in the existing game.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` completed without errors.

### Active
- Browser-check the game and challenge flow; screenshot verification remains to be done.

### Blocked
- Initial Playwright launch failed because Chromium was not installed. `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` subsequently completed, so browser verification can now be retried.

## Next Move
1. Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` and verify the game renders and starts.
2. Test jump, movement, K double-tap, and lobby behavior (ideally in two tabs).
3. Save and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay mechanics, lobby discovery, and duel message handling.
- `index.html`: lobby UI, controls, and game HUD.
- `styles.css`: lobby and responsive control styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; none have been committed or pushed.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The online lobby uses `BroadcastChannel('ring-riot-lobby-v1')`; it only discovers same-origin tabs/windows in a compatible browser.

## Objective
- Expand RING//RIOT into a playable fighting game with triple jumps, faster movement, double-tap K spin kicks, face uploads, and a lobby to find and challenge players.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use `BroadcastChannel` for browser-local fighter discovery and duels; this is not internet-wide multiplayer.
- Keep CPU fights as the default and add challenges through the lobby.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added triple-jump physics, faster movement, double-tap K spin kicks, and touch controls.
- Added a lobby with player presence, challenge/accept flow, and duel state/damage messages.
- Added lobby/control styling; face upload was already present.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Browser opened the game, rendered its UI, and started a fight; jump and K inputs were exercised.
- Saved and inspected `screenshots/ring-riot-check.jpg`.

### Active
- Complete browser verification, especially the challenge/accept flow across two tabs and checking for console errors or gameplay issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test lobby discovery and challenge acceptance in two tabs.
2. Check control and gameplay behavior, inspect console output, and address any issues.
3. Re-run syntax/diff checks after fixes.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: gameplay mechanics, lobby discovery, and duel message handling.
- `index.html`: lobby UI, controls, and game HUD.
- `styles.css`: lobby and responsive control styling.
- `screenshots/ring-riot-check.jpg`: latest browser-check screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; none have been committed or pushed.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser URL is `http://localhost:3002`.
- The lobby uses `BroadcastChannel('ring-riot-lobby-v1')` and only discovers compatible same-origin tabs/windows.
